editorial.headline: Textile and Fashion Design: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A broad design activity spanning textiles, garments, accessories and jewellery, open nationally to full foreign ownership but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the industrial design of textile, fashion and garment products, including work carried out through specialised software. Its practical canvas is wide: fabric and woven goods, crocheted products, clothing and underwear, headwear, footwear, socks, stockings and laces all sit within it. So do designs for bags, suitcases and cases; ties, shawls, scarves and handkerchiefs; gloves, umbrellas, walking sticks and fans; ribbons, hair ties, clothing accessories and other adornments; and jewellery. The common thread is design: the activity concerns creating the product design rather than describing a particular retail or manufacturing operation.

It is open across the full business-scale range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, the position is straightforward. The activity is TERBUKA to foreign investment, and the maximum foreign ownership is 100%. In other words, the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity; there is no lower foreign-ownership ceiling stated in the record.

Bali changes that answer decisively for a foreign-owned registration. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Low or Medium-Low across every part of the stated scope. That places the activity within Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, introduced on May 13, 2026. The restriction is therefore not a reduced ownership percentage or a local-partnership condition: it is a block on PMA registration in Bali under the province’s risk-based moratorium.

That distinction matters. The national setting remains open to 100% foreign ownership, but it does not override Bali’s separate provincial position. For a founder considering this activity, the honest reading is two-layered: the activity is nationally available to foreign investment at every listed scale, while Bali’s recorded risk classification makes PMA registration unavailable on the island. The national openness is real; so is the Bali block.
